results.title: Manchester Population Density-Copy
results.description:
Census data reveals that population density varies noticeably from area to area. Small area census data do a better job depicting how where the crowded neighborhoods are. 

In this map, the yellow areas of highest density range from 30,000 to 150,000 persons per square kilometer. In those areas, if the people were spread out evenly across the area, there would be just 4 to 9 meters between them. Very high density areas exceed 7,000 persons per square kilometer. High density areas exceed 5,200 persons per square kilometer. The last categories break at 3,330 persons per square kilometer, and 1,500 persons per square kilometer. 

This map was created using Census 2011 data combined with Ordnance Survey's Open Boundaries and Ordnance Survey Open Map Local's Buildings layer.

How to make this map for your city

results.title: UPRN PoC Web Map Greater Manchester v1.1
results.description:
This Web Map contains datasets from multiple data providers, such as Ordnance Survey (OS), United Kingdom Centre for Ecology & Hydrology (UKCEH), Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (DEFRA), Met Office, etc. to provide a proof-of-concept solution for a service that enables streamlined access to government geospatial data through querying on the Unique Property Reference Number (UPRN) level. Users are able to select UPRNs and access the values from the underlying datasets.

The service contains the following data groups:
  • UPRN points
  • Administrative areas
  • Environmental variables from the ClimateJust project
  • Noise pollution data from DEFRA
  • Modelled background pollution data from DEFRA
  • Carbon storage and water supply data from UKCEH
  • Ellenberg Vegetation Indicator data from UKCEH
  • Multiple datasets from Met Office's Air Quality Reanalysis datasets
The above datasets, combined with Ordnance Survey's most up-to-date UPRN register, comprise the basis of an efficient workflow for acquiring localised pollution, vegetation, and administrative information. This, in turn, provides decision makers with enhanced and granular understanding of the connection of different phenomena, resulting in more informed actions on any scale from national to local.
results.snippet: Web Map containing the Proof of Concept Unique Property Reference Number (UPRN) Service for Greater Manchester. It integrates and presents data from several agencies in an easily queriable way, enabling users to access environmental and administrative information on the UPRN level.

results.title: Carbon Storage Web Map (Greater Manchester)
results.description: This data set contains UK-wide maps of ten different among-model ensemble approaches for two services: above ground Carbon stock and water supply. The data for Carbon comes as fourteen TIF maps for above ground carbon storage at a 1-km2 resolution with associated world files: ten approaches, with a double option for two of those, together with maps of variation among models and among ensembles. For water, the data comes as one shapefile with polygons per watershed, each polygon containing these fourteen estimates. For all maps, 600dpi jpg depictions are added to the supporting information. Directory location independent layer files are included to aid scaling and providing the colour palettes. Ensemble output maps were calculated with different approaches following the supporting documentation and associated publication. Uncertainty estimates for these services are included as variation among contributing model outputs and among the employed ensemble approaches. The work was completed under the ‘EnsemblES - Using ensemble techniques to capture the accuracy and sensitivity of ecosystem service models’ project (NE/T00391X/1) funded by the UKRI Landscape Decisions programme. Full details about this dataset can be found at https://doi.org/10.5285/a9ae773d-b742-4d42-ae42-2b594bae5d38
results.snippet: Carbon Storage Web Map (Greater Manchester)

results.title: Public Transport Accessibility, Household Vehicle Accessibility, and Unemployment - Greater Manchester
results.description: The links between personal mobility and employment has long been an area of concern across Transport Geography and Planning literature, often informing transport policy (Johnson et al., 2017). To this end, it is helpful to understand the spatiality of different transport and employment needs – Are there areas of high employment and low car ownership centred around public transit? Or areas of transport exclusion with high unemployment? This map, therefore, aims to communicate the relationship between public transport (PT) accessibility, household vehicle access, and employment across Greater Manchester.
results.snippet: Mapping the relationship between public transport accessibility, household vehicle accessibility, and unemployment.

results.title: Political walking and the picturesque
results.description:
Through a range of picturesque and political walking data, this map explores different modes of engagement with The Peak District. Gilpin’s tour is presented as points as his emphasis is on picturesque vistas. Whereas the movement between Gilpin’s sites is negligible, the walking routes taken by the Trespassers and Black Girls Hike (BGH) is the substance of their engagement, people being in and moving through the land. BGH continues the trespasser’s legacy of political walking, building confidence in black women who may feel unwelcome in predominantly white middleclass outdoor spaces. In an interesting tension with the picturesque BGH also emphasises the visual: representing black women in the countryside so that others see this space as accessible. For BGH, the political power of people in the landscape is far from Gilpin’s aesthetic amorality. Similarly, pictures of the trespassers helped build support for the right to roam movement. The political walking shown combines experiential movement and visual representation, complicating a purely picturesque landscape. All three sources are about bringing people to The Peaks, whether that be picturesque tourism or rambling. The paradox of people engaging more with the landscape is that whilst it increases environmentalism it also increases risk of wildlife damage. The high frequency of wildfires on Kinder Scout demonstrates this increased engagement and increased risk. This landscape, with such a strong history of political walking, demonstrates that a new form of political, environmentally engaged, walking must emerge for the landscape’s posterity in the age of the climate crisis.

<o:p></o:p>
results.snippet: Through a range of picturesque and political walking data, this map explores different modes of engagement with The Peak District.

results.title: Brexit voting by region
results.description: In light of Brexit negotiations once again reaching a stalemate, I decided to map the relationship between disposable income and referendum results across the national scale. A bivariate choropleth map was used to illustrate the relationship. The expected outcome was that areas with low disposable incomes would have a lower percentage of remain votes whilst the opposite would be true for areas of high disposable income.
results.snippet: This map illustrates the relationship between disposable income and and results of the 2016 EU Referendum.

results.title: Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) 2019
results.description:
The English Indices of Deprivation 2019 use 39 separate indicators, organised across seven distinct domains of deprivation which can be combined, using appropriate weights, to calculate the Index of Multiple Deprivation 2019 (IMD 2019). This is an overall measure of multiple deprivation experienced by people living in an area and is calculated for every Lower layer Super Output Area (LSOA) in England. The IMD 2019 can be used to rank every LSOA in England according to their relative level of deprivation.

results.title: Literary Landscapes Formative Assessment
results.snippet: Jane Austen utilised walking as a mode of political rebellion in the 1913 novel Pride and Prejudice. A woman walking outside alone was more than an act of convenience; it was an act of rebellion against both the physical constraints of a petticoat, and the social constraints of walking without a chaperone or walking with purpose at all. Mapped is Lizzie’s three-mile walk to Netherfield to tend to her ailing sister. (Using John Cary’s ‘A new map of Hertfordshire’ created in 1801.)  The reaction to Lizzie’s exertion is extreme, from mockery to alarm. Mrs Bennet exclaims, “You will not be fit to be seen when you get there.”  Ironically, the focus is on her appearance rather than her safety. Using a visual aid to map Lizzies walk makes clear, the absurdity that an hour walk would receive such a reaction. Mr Darcey questions, “to walk three miles, or four miles, or five miles, or whatever it is, above her ankles in dirt, and alone, quite alone! What could she mean by it?”  Walking with purpose was considered a masculine act or even associated with poverty. Therefore, women of a higher class were expected only to promenade to be seen or stroll to admire the picturesque. To walk with the intention to travel rather than be observed is an act of postfeminist rebellion from Lizzie, as the folly reactions of Mr Darcey and Mrs Bennet to a simple walk, as the map reveals, was a rebellious act from Austen.

results.name: Carbon_Storage_Up_the_Distinct_Ensemble
results.title: Carbon Storage (GM) - Up the Distinct Ensemble
results.description: Distinct model types emphasising models that may contain processes not captured in others, or by penalising those models that go against the convention (Grenouillet et al. 2011). Attribute weighting could be done for many attributes, which are largely arbitrary in use. To not focus on one attribute but many at the same them we choose an overall attribute assessment into groups based on 17 categories per model. The grouping statistic used is a pairwise Spearman’s rank correlation among binary classifications. The work was completed under the ‘EnsemblES - Using ensemble techniques to capture the accuracy and sensitivity of ecosystem service models’ project (NE/T00391X/1) funded by the UKRI Landscape Decisions programme. Full details about this dataset can be found at https://doi.org/10.5285/a9ae773d-b742-4d42-ae42-2b594bae5d38

High density areas exceed 5,200 persons per square kilometer. The last categories break at 3,330 persons per square kilometer, and 1,500 persons per square kilometer.

results.name: Carbon_Storage_Leave_one_out_Cross_validation_Ensemble
results.title: Carbon Storage (GM) - Leave-one-out Cross-validation Ensemble
results.description: It is our second iterative consensus approach following direct recommendation in Dormann et al. (2018), with the difference of not omitting sets of data points but entire models one-by-one. As for the above this is done using a no constant multi-variation regression with the same nlmefit-tool, with the same settings and naïve priors. However, in this approach we loop through the model outputs. One-by-one, a regression is performed using a single model output as comparator and the remaining model outputs as explanatory variables. The work was completed under the ‘EnsemblES - Using ensemble techniques to capture the accuracy and sensitivity of ecosystem service models’ project (NE/T00391X/1) funded by the UKRI Landscape Decisions programme. Full details about this dataset can be found at https://doi.org/10.5285/a9ae773d-b742-4d42-ae42-2b594bae5d38

results.name: Carbon_Storage_PCA_Ensemble
results.title: Carbon Storage (GM) - PCA Ensemble
results.description: PCA as consensus axis, being a deterministic approach. The suggestion of using PCA’s comes from Marmion et al. (2009) and Grenouillet et al. (2011). Deterministic here means that the result is an inherent property of the dataset, i.e. the statistical outcome is identical given the same dataset. Principal components were calculated using the Matlab princomp-tool, the weights per model i outputted to Eq. 1 were the loadings to the first –main– pca axis. So models with the better correlation to the consensus axis are assigned higher weights. The work was completed under the ‘EnsemblES - Using ensemble techniques to capture the accuracy and sensitivity of ecosystem service models’ project (NE/T00391X/1) funded by the UKRI Landscape Decisions programme. Full details about this dataset can be found at https://doi.org/10.5285/a9ae773d-b742-4d42-ae42-2b594bae5d38

results.description:
‘Listing’ is the all-encompassing term for the legal protection given to a building, monument, structure or site through the planning system. It is recognition of historical, architectural or archaeological significance, intended to ensure that the character of the asset in question is preserved for future generations. The main types of Listing are:
  • Listed Buildings
  • Scheduled Monuments
  • Registered Parks and Gardens
  • Registered Battlefields
  • Protected Wreck Sites
  • World Heritage Sites

Data is updated daily.

Further details are available on our website here - https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/

Historic England Open Data Hub - https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/open-data-hub/

Field descriptions

Listed Buildings

Field name Field alias Description
List Entry List entry number List Entry Number: unique reference number from the National Heritage List for England
Name Name Name of building
Grade Grade Grade of building; in descending order of importance: I, II*,II
ListDate Listing date Date on which the building was added to the Statutory List of Buildings
AmendDate Amendment date Date on which the listing was last amended
CaptureScale Capture scale Scale at which the spatial representation of that listed building was captured
hyperlink NHLE link URL of the record on the Historic England website

Building Preservation Notices

Field name Field alias Description
List Entry List entry number List Entry Number: unique reference number from the National Heritage List for England
Name Name Name of building
BPNStart Building Preservation Notice start date Start date of the notice
BPNExpire Building Preservation Notice expiry date Expiry date of the notice
CaptureScale Capture scale Scale at which the spatial representation of that building preservation notice was captured
hyperlink NHLE link URL of the record on the Historic England website

Certificates of Immunity

Field name Field alias Description
List Entry List entry number List Entry Number: unique reference number from the National Heritage List for England
Name Name Name of building
COIStart Certificate of Immunity start date Start date of the certificate
COIExpire Certificate of Immunity expiry date Expiry date of the certificate
CaptureScale Capture scale Scale at which the spatial representation of that certificate of immunity was captured
hyperlink NHLE link URL of the record on the Historic England website

Scheduled Monuments

Field name Field alias Description
List Entry List entry number List Entry Number: unique reference number from the National Heritage List for England
Name Name Statutory registered title of monument
SchedDate Schedule date Date on which the monument was included in the Schedule of Monuments
AmendDate Amendment date Date on which the scheduling was last amended
CaptureScale Capture scale Scale at which the spatial representation of that scheduled monument was captured
hyperlink NHLE link URL of the record on the Historic England website
area_ha Area (ha) Area of the polygon in hectares

Registered Parks and Gardens

Field name Field alias Description
List Entry List entry number List Entry Number: unique reference number from the National Heritage List for England
Name Name Registered title of park and garden
Grade Grade Grade of park and garden; in descending order of importance: I, II*, II
RegDate Registration date Date on which the park and garden was included in the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens
AmendDate Amendment date Date on which the registration was last amended
CaptureScale Capture scale Scale at which the spatial representation of that park and garden was captured
hyperlink NHLE link URL of the record on the Historic England website
area_ha Area (ha) Area of the polygon in hectares

Registered Battlefields

Field name Field alias Description
List Entry List entry number List Entry Number: unique reference number from the National Heritage List for England
Name Name Registered title of battlefield
RegDate Registration date Date on which the battlefield was included in the Register of Historic Battlefields
AmendDate Amendment date Date on which the registration was last amended
CaptureScale Capture scale Scale at which the spatial representation of that battlefield was captured
hyperlink NHLE link URL of the record on the Historic England website
area_ha Area (ha) Area of the polygon in hectares

Protected Wreck Sites

Field name Field alias Description
List Entry List entry number List Entry Number: unique reference number from the National Heritage List for England
Name Name Name of wreck site
DesigDate Designation date Date on which the wreck site was designated as a restricted area
AmendDate Amendment date Date on which the designation was last amended
CaptureScale Capture scale Scale at which the spatial representation of that protected wreck was captured
hyperlink NHLE link URL of the record on the Historic England website
area_ha Area (ha) Area of the polygon in hectares

World Heritage Sites

Field name Field alias Description
List Entry List entry number List Entry Number: unique reference number from the National Heritage List for England
Name Name Title of world heritage property
InscrDate Inscription date Date on which the property was inscribed on the World Heritage List by UNESCO
AmendDate Amendment date Date on which the inscription was last amended
Notes Notes Denotes if polygon is Property Boundary (noted as Core Area) or Buffer Zone
CaptureScale Capture scale Scale at which the spatial representation of that World Heritage Site was captured
hyperlink NHLE link URL of the record on the Historic England website
area_ha Area (ha) Area of the polygon in hectares
results.snippet: The National Heritage List for England (NHLE) is the only official, up to date, register of all nationally protected historic buildings and sites in England - listed buildings, scheduled monuments, protected wrecks, registered parks and gardens, and battlefields.Data is updated daily.
